title: Month-grouped session layout; per-user gated on 2+ participants
decision: Session document discovery uses iter_session_documents() to read legacy flat session files (sessions/YYYY-MM-DD.md), new month-grouped flat files (sessions/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md), and new month-grouped per-user files (sessions/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD/<user>.md). Per-user layout activates only when 2+ participants are registered.
why: Month grouping organizes session history by calendar period for better discoverability; per-user gating prevents fragmentation for single-user projects while supporting team workflows when participants are declared.
evolution: Founded from the control file; no session lineage attached yet.
source_quote: Session document discovery: package readers use `iter_session_documents()` in `core.py` to read legacy flat session files (`sessions/YYYY-MM-DD.md`), legacy per-day/per-user files (`sessions/YYYY-MM-DD/<user>.md`), new month-grouped flat files (`sessions/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`), and new month-grouped per-user files (`sessions/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD/<user>.md`).

supporting.quote: The migration parses each legacy `sessions/YYYY-MM-DD.md` entry, maps entry `user_initials` through `.memory-seed/project.yaml` `participants:`, writes/appends to `sessions/YYYY-MM-DD/<user>.md`

title: Deterministic 80-bit mse_ ids; legacy ms- never rewritten
decision: New generated session entry_id values use deterministic 80-bit mse_ IDs encoded in 16 lower-case Base32 characters. Legacy ms- IDs remain valid forever and are never rewritten.
why: 80 bits is the practical middle ground for collision risk at team scale, materially shorter than 128-bit visible IDs, and negligible collision risk for plausible Memory Seed corpora. Preserving legacy IDs maintains append-only immutability and backward compatibility.
evolution: Evolved in mse_77cn2v0rg9na3w0v:d1 where generate_session_entry_id() was implemented to emit deterministic mse_ IDs using SHA-256 and Crockford/Base32 alphabet.
source_quote: Entry-ID widening + MCP metadata filters (shipped 2.12.0): new generated session `entry_id` values use deterministic 80-bit `mse_` IDs while legacy `ms-` IDs remain valid and are never rewritten.

supporting.quote: New generated entry IDs are planned as `mse_` plus 80 bits encoded in 16 lower-case Base32 characters; legacy `ms-` IDs remain valid forever.

title: DRAFT single-decision baseline; D/R mandatory; numbered decisions canonical
decision: The single-decision DRAFT record is the baseline session-entry shape. D/R (Decision/Rationale) are mandatory fields; A/F/T (Alternatives/Findings/Tests) are optional. Multi-decision entries use numbered #### Dn headings as the canonical form.
why: A baseline structure with mandatory decision rationale ensures every memory entry captures the core reasoning. Explicit numbering makes multi-decision entries unambiguous and discoverable.
evolution: Founded from the control file; established as baseline in 2.4.0 per the control plane history.
source_quote: The single-decision DRAFT record is the **baseline** session-entry shape (since 2.4.0); the bare summary (simpler) and multi-decision (richer) shapes are explicit routes off it. D/R are mandatory, A/F/T optional.

title: Branch-session fuse: branch-only, chronological, immutable relative to base
decision: memory-seed session fuse --branch <branch> dry-runs and applies branch-local session entries and diagram sidecars. Imported entries must be branch-only, chronological, immutable relative to base, and carry `branch: <branch>` metadata.
why: Chronological immutability relative to the base preserves append-only ordering when merging branch work. The branch metadata enables recovery and validation during structured fuse.
evolution: Founded from the control file; implements the structural session merge capability.
source_quote: Branch-session fuse (current unreleased worktree): `memory-seed session fuse --branch <branch>` dry-runs branch-local session entries and diagram sidecars before promotion, and `--apply` writes only during an in-progress `git merge --no-ff --no-commit <branch>`. Imported entries must be branch-only, chronological, immutable relative to base, and carry `branch: <branch>`.

title: session merge-branch is the one-step integration primitive, not a git merge driver
decision: memory-seed session merge-branch --branch <branch> wraps fuse dry-run, git merge --no-ff --no-commit, session-path reset, fuse apply, staging, and merge commit into one command. It fails closed: fuse issues abort before any merge state exists; requires a clean working tree.
why: One-step integration prevents manual skipping of fuse steps that previously led to out-of-order session entries landing via raw git line-merges. Failing closed on fuse issues ensures no corrupted merge state.
evolution: Founded from the control file; implemented after incidents where manual fuse steps were skipped.
source_quote: One-step branch integration (current unreleased worktree): `memory-seed session merge-branch --branch <branch> [--dry-run]` wraps fuse dry-run, `git merge --no-ff --no-commit`, session-path reset to base content, fuse apply, staging, and the merge commit into one command, added after two incidents where the manual fuse steps were skipped and raw git line-merges landed session entries out of chronological order. Fails closed: fuse issues abort before any merge state exists.

title: Configurable integration_mode: local-merge vs PR
decision: integration_mode is a project-local default read fail-open as local-merge, surfaced by ESR, obeyed by live+seed agent contracts, and implemented by mode-aware session integrate plus session open-pr.
why: Different workflows require different integration strategies: local-merge for single-developer rapid iteration, PR for team review gates. Configurable mode lets projects choose without code changes.
evolution: Founded from the control file; completed 2026-07-15 per the control plane history.
source_quote: Configurable integration mode (completed 2026-07-15): `integration_mode: local-merge|pr` is a project-local default read fail-open as `local-merge`, surfaced by ESR, obeyed by live+seed agent contracts, and implemented by mode-aware `session integrate` plus `session open-pr`.

title: Forward-only authoring with read-time bidirectional traversal
decision: related-entries edges are authored forward-only in source entry YAML. Bidirectional traversal happens at read time by computing inbound backlinks from all resolvable outbound refs. No historical entries are rewritten.
why: Forward-only authoring with read-time inversion preserves append-only without ever editing a historical entry. This gives the old-to-new relationship view without breaking immutability.
evolution: Evolved in mse_a67jnwa1048dn3wc:d1 where bidirectional read-time traversal was chosen over sidecar files, preserving Markdown as single source of truth.
source_quote: Forward-only authoring + read-time bidirectional traversal preserves append-only; backfill between pre-existing entries and an optional `link add` writer are deferred (P2).

supporting.quote: Settled the four open decisions (bidirectional read-time traversal of directed forward edges; backfill between pre-existing entries out of 3.0 scope)

title: Model2Vec default provider; silent lexical degrade; model2vec the only required dep
decision: model2vec (minishlab/potion-base-8M) is a REQUIRED dependency and the package's only one. pip install --no-deps memory-seed is the supported lightweight install. MCP memory search uses Model2Vec by default and falls back to lexical, metadata, and recency ranking if semantic scoring fails or is disabled.
why: Model2Vec provides deterministic semantic ranking without external APIs. Silent fallback to lexical ranking tolerates provider unavailability without breaking core functionality. Single required dep keeps the core package minimal.
evolution: Founded from the control file; reaffirmed in control plane versions 2.11 onwards.
source_quote: `model2vec` is a REQUIRED dependency and the package's only one; `pip install --no-deps memory-seed` is the supported lightweight install without semantic ranking.

supporting.quote: MCP memory search uses the Model2Vec static embedding provider `model2vec:minishlab/potion-base-8M` by default and falls back to lexical, metadata, and recency ranking

title: Non-destructive routing into foreign entry-point files
decision: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, .github/copilot-instructions.md follow a 4-way ownership branch: greenfield writes full seed file; ours (has memory-system-version frontmatter) archive+replace version-gated; foreign with markers re-sync managed block in place; foreign without markers inject marker-delimited routing block. Foreign files are never overwritten.
why: Sub-projects may inherit Memory Seed but own their own entry-point routing files. Non-destructive injection preserves foreign content while wiring up the seed system.
evolution: Founded from the control file; implemented in 2.8.0 per the control plane history.
source_quote: Non-destructive routing into foreign entry-point files (2.8.0): the four routing files follow a 4-way ownership branch: greenfield → write full seed file; ours → version-gated archive+replace; foreign with our markers → re-sync the managed block in place; foreign without markers → inject a marker-delimited routing block
